newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks active but expected to slow.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks active but expected to slow.

text.p: Croatian stocks burst into life on Tuesday in a mixed market, but traders said activity was likely to tail off in the coming weeks and a possible U.S. rate rise could be a factor.

"Interest rates in the United States are expected to rise which means less investment and lower prices in the emerging markets of Eastern and Central Europe," Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage told Reuters.
He said most U.S. investors were holding back pending the new decision on interest rates due on May 21.
"There is an evident lack of investors," Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage said, adding it was hard to foresee how long the trend would last.
Eight of 15 active issues fell and seven rose with volume rising fivefold from Friday to 15,692 shares and turnover tenfold to 14.2 million kuna.

Varteks, Croatia's biggest textile company, led the day's gainers. It added 8.1 percent to 80 kuna on the back of reports that U.S. clothing giant Levi Strauss & Co. had renewed its licence to produce Levi's jeans.
Levi's earlier threatened to pull out unless the company was privatised before the end of June.
"I think this stock will see lots of ups and downs, but the news is likely to spark some growth initially," said Pavletic.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares and Pliva pharmaceutical accounted for most of the day's activity.
Pliva was the most actively traded stock with 5,272 units sold. It closed one kuna lower, at the bottom of a 475-480 kuna range, and traders predicted no major changes soon.

Zagrebacka led the day's losers, dropping 40 kuna to 2,160 on volume of 3,778 shares after its 1/10 GDRs on London Seaq bottomed at $35, the lowest in the past two weeks. They later recovered to $35.125.
"It seems demand (for Zagrebacka) is stronger here now than in London," said Pavletic. "Its price will probably drop a bit tomorrow, but should rebound soon," he added.
The bank's E series preference stocks added 35 kuna to 1,060 kuna on volume of 726 shares.
Another fully listed stock, Varazdinska Banka ordinary shares, rose 900 kuna to 45,900, but it only sold 27 units.
Food processor Podravka closed one kuna lower at 304 kuna after trading in a 300-306 kuna range with 2,889 shares sold.
Chocolate maker Kras gained ten kuna to 425 trading 275 units.
